key_insight: You can learn a compact, controllable action space directly from uncurated videos (no action labels) and use it to build world models that predict consequences of latent actions in the wild.
problem_solved: World models typically require explicit action labels and curated data; this work addresses how to learn actionable, disentangled control representations from in-the-wild videos without supervised action annotations.
method: Self-supervised video modeling that separates controllable factors (latent actions) from passive/environmental factors using a structured encoder and dynamics prior.
Training objectives that enforce action-consistency (e.g., inverse/contrastive or cycle-consistency losses) and enable action-conditioned prediction in latent space.
Use the learned latent-action world model for planning or rollout by decoding latent action sequences to predicted observations, enabling downstream control or evaluation without labeled actions.
impact: Enables scalable learning of model-based control and planning from large unlabeled video corpora, reducing reliance on costly action annotations and accelerating transfer to robotics, simulation, and embodied AI tasks.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: raw video → encoder → split latents (action vs context) → latent dynamics → decoded predicted frames
Latent-action manifold visualization (2D projection) showing discrete/continuous action clusters discovered from diverse videos
Qualitative rollouts: side-by-side actual vs action-conditioned predicted frames across a few real-world clips
Bar chart or table comparing performance: supervised-action world model vs learned-latent-action model on prediction/planning metrics
paper_title: Learning Latent Action World Models In The Wild
paper_authors: Quentin Garrido, Tushar Nagarajan, Basile Terver, Nicolas Ballas, Yann LeCun
